steps.question: Do the 16 heart samples (WT-vehicle, WT-drug, KO-vehicle, KO-drug; n=4 each) separate by genotype and treatment on PCA, and are library sizes and sample-to-sample distances consistent with the declared design, with no outlier sample or unexpected batch structure?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC (blind VST-equivalent, PCA on top 500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap) per R-0033@40bf before any model is fit

steps.description: Load counts.csv (12000 genes x samples) and metadata.csv (16 samples x genotype/treatment/condition), reconcile sample sets between the two files (report and set aside any counts.csv column absent from metadata.csv), compute PyDESeq2 size factors, apply a variance-stabilizing-equivalent log-transform, run PCA on the top 500 most-variable genes, plot a sample-distance heatmap, and plot library size per sample, colored by genotype and by treatment.
acceptance_criteria: PCA plot and sample-distance heatmap produced, colored by genotype and by treatment
Library size barplot produced for all reconciled samples
Any mismatch between counts.csv sample columns and metadata.csv rows is explicitly reported (count and identity)

steps.name: PyDESeq2 interaction model: simple effects and interaction contrast
steps.question: Using the reconciled 16-sample cohort, is there a genotype x treatment interaction in heart gene expression (design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, reference genotype=WT, reference treatment=vehicle), and what are the drug-vs-vehicle effects separately in WT and in KO?

grounding.reason: DESeq2/PyDESeq2 interaction design with explicit reference levels, Wald test on the interaction coefficient plus the two simple effects, ashr shrinkage for non-single-coefficient contrasts, per R-0013@2639 and R-0092@bb58

constraints: min_count=10, min_samples=4 (smallest group size) pre-filter; do not over-filter beyond this — independent filtering at the results step does the rest
design_terms = genotype, treatment, genotype:treatment with explicit reference levels genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle
shrink_lfc must use ashr (not apeglm) for the KO simple effect and the interaction contrast, since these are not single model coefficients
BH adjustment with independent filtering on, alpha=0.05, applied within each of the three contrasts separately
steps.description: Pre-filter genes to >=10 counts in >=4 samples (the smallest cell size). Fit PyDESeq2 with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, explicit reference levels genotype=WT and treatment=vehicle. Extract three Wald results per gene: (a) drug vs vehicle in WT (the treatment main-effect coefficient), (b) drug vs vehicle in KO (main effect + interaction coefficient, built as a contrast), (c) the interaction coefficient itself (genotypeKO.treatmentdrug), i.e. the difference-of-differences. Apply ashr shrinkage (via rpy2 call into R's ashr, since the KO simple effect and interaction term are contrasts of coefficients, not single coefficients that apeglm could handle) to each of the three result sets, keeping both shrunken and unshrunken log2FoldChange plus lfcSE in the output tables. Flag any gene with an NA p-value from Cook's-distance count-outlier detection (expected behavior at n=4/cell, below the 7-replicate threshold where DESeq2 imputes instead) separately from genes removed by independent filtering. Produce MA and dispersion diagnostic plots for the fitted model.
acceptance_criteria: Three named result tables produced: WT drug-vs-vehicle, KO drug-vs-vehicle, interaction contrast
Each table reports unshrunken log2FoldChange, ashr-shrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, Wald stat, p-value, and BH-adjusted p-value
Reference levels (genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle) stated in the output metadata
Count of genes with NA p-values from the outlier flag reported separately from independent-filtering exclusions
MA plot and dispersion plot saved for the fitted model
Number of genes tested after pre-filtering and number significant (padj<0.05) per contrast reported

gsea_input = full ranked list of tested genes, never a thresholded subset

steps.description: For each of the three DESeq2/PyDESeq2 result tables from T1S2, rank all tested genes (post pre-filter) by the Wald statistic and run gseapy prerank against the MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC symbols) and then against the Reactome human pathway gene sets, each with a minimum set size of 15 and a maximum of 500 genes among the tested genes as the universe. steps.description: Assemble a single report combining: the three DESeq2/PyDESeq2 result tables (WT drug effect, KO drug effect, interaction contrast) with shrunken and unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, and padj; the MA and dispersion diagnostic plots; the count of genes tested, genes significant per contrast, and genes flagged NA by the count-outlier rule; the six GSEA tables (Hallmark and Reactome x three contrasts) with leading-edge genes for significant sets; an explicit p-value histogram check per contrast before trusting the BH adjustment; and a reproducibility record (PyDESeq2/ashr/gseapy versions, gene-set collection versions and dates, random seeds). acceptance_criteria: Report states the reference levels, all three contrasts by name, and their result counts side by side
Report explicitly separates statistically supported interaction findings from qualitative divergence between simple effects that did not reach interaction significance
Power limitation of the interaction test at n=4/cell is stated explicitly, not implied
Reproducibility record (versions, seeds, gene-set collection dates) included
MA plot, dispersion plot, and p-value histograms per contrast included

plan.title: Heart 2x2 genotype x drug interaction DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: The research question is whether the drug acts differently in KO vs WT heart tissue — a genotype x treatment interaction question on a 2x2 factorial (WT/KO x vehicle/drug, n=4/cell, 17 files listed but metadata.csv declares 16 samples x 4 columns; the analysis uses the 16 samples in metadata.csv as authoritative and flags any counts.csv column not present in metadata). Raw Salmon gene-level counts (12000 genes x samples) are modeled directly in PyDESeq2 with a full interaction design (~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment), because the interaction coefficient — not either main effect alone — answers the stated question: whether the treatment effect differs by genotype. Per Inflexa's DESeq2/PyDESeq2 procedure for a 2x2 interaction design with 4 replicates per cell: (1) QC sample structure first via PCA/sample-distance on a variance-stabilized matrix to catch outliers or batch drift before any model is fit; (2) minimal low-count pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=4 samples, the smallest cell size), leaving DESeq2's own independent filtering at the results stage to do the rest; (3) fit the interaction model with explicit reference levels (genotype=WT, treatment=vehicle) so every coefficient has a stated, reproducible meaning; (4) test three things side by side per Inflexa's interaction-reporting rule — the drug effect in WT (reference), the drug effect in KO, and the interaction contrast itself — because the interaction term alone has low power at n=4/cell and does not by itself say whether the drug does anything in either genotype; (5) shrink log2 fold changes with ashr (not apeglm) because the KO simple effect and the interaction term are contrasts of coefficients, not single model coefficients, which is outside apeglm's scope; (6) BH-adjust p-values within each of the three contrasts separately, with independent filtering on and a p-value histogram check before trusting the adjustment; (7) run preranked GSEA (gseapy) per contrast against MSigDB Hallmark (confirmed staged) then Reactome (confirmed staged) using the Wald statistic as the ranking metric, since with 12000 genes tested a handful of significant genes from an underpowered interaction test would give an over-representation test no power — the ranked method finds coordinated small effects that no single gene shows; (8) a final report step assembles the three-contrast table, fit diagnostics (MA/dispersion plots), leading-edge genes per significant pathway, and a full reproducibility record (package versions, seeds, gene-set collection versions). All scripts are Python per the user's constraint; PyDESeq2 (0.5.4) plus ashr (called from Python via rpy2, both confirmed installed) implement the DESeq2-equivalent statistics, and gseapy (1.3.1) implements the preranked enrichment against the confirmed-staged human Hallmark and Reactome GMTs.
